panels.description: Cluster-wide count of distinct users with at least one active socket on any switchboard pod (sourced from Redis, refreshed on every pod every 30s). Aggregated with max() to collapse the per-pod samples (which should agree) into a single line.
panels.title: Active Users

panels.description: Error rate for authentications against App Suite MW
panels.title: Authentication error rate
Errors (E): The number of failed requests
Duration (D): The amount of time to process a request

panels.description: Per-pod auth failure rate broken down by reason label (jose error code or category, e.g. ERR_JWT_EXPIRED).
panels.title: Authentication errors by reason

panels.description: p95 duration of JWT verification (includes JWKS fetch on cache miss).
panels.title: JWT verify p95 latency

panels.description: Per-pod rate of JWT verification failures.
panels.title: JWT verify error rate

panels.description: Current websocket connections on each pod (socket_io_connected gauge).
panels.title: Sockets connected (per pod)

panels.description: Per-pod websocket connect events per second (derived from socket_io_connect_total counter).
panels.title: Socket connect rate (per pod)

panels.description: Per-pod websocket disconnect events per second (derived from socket_io_disconnect_total counter).
panels.title: Socket disconnect rate (per pod)

panels.description: Bull delayedOfflineState queue depth by state. 'completed' should stay near zero — if it climbs monotonically, jobs are being moved to the completed set instead of removed, which is the canonical Bull leak signature. 'delayed' is the in-flight grace-window count and tracks current concurrent-disconnect rate. 'active' should be transient.
panels.title: Bull delayedOfflineState — queue depth by state

panels.description: Number of Redis keys matching each per-user pattern written by switchboard. availability:* / lastSeen:* / availabilityVisibility:* are written by the offline worker and presence-change handlers, but never deleted. If they grow monotonically with no plateau, that's the per-user-key leak.
panels.title: Redis keys by pattern

panels.description: Pending commands in each ioredis client's send queue, per pod. Per-pod (not aggregated), because back-pressure on one pod's connection is what matters. A growing queue precedes a buffer overflow / dropped connection.
panels.title: ioredis command queue (per pod / role)

panels.description: Prune passes over the last 15 minutes, summed over all pods. Every pod tries a pass every 5 minutes and only the lock holder runs it, so ok should stay at 3. error means not every switchboard on the Redis pub/sub channel answered within 5 seconds: a slow replica, old replicas during a rollout, or another switchboard deployment sharing the same Redis. Orphaned sockets then wait for the next successful pass. Passes skipped because another pod holds the lock are left out.
panels.title: Prune passes by result (per 15m)

panels.description: How long a successful prune pass takes, including collecting socket ids from all replicas. Grows with the number of registered sockets and connected users.
panels.title: Prune pass duration

panels.description: Socket registrations the prune pass removed because no replica holds the socket anymore. A spike after a pod restart is expected, removed on the second pass after the restart. A steady baseline means sockets leak some other way.
panels.title: Orphaned sockets removed (per 15m)

panels.description: Connected users without any socket for two prune passes, queued for their offline job. High for a few passes after the first deploy with this metric while the backlog is cleaned up (at most 5,000 per pass), then near zero. A steady rise means offline jobs keep getting lost.
panels.title: Stale users cleaned up (per 15m)

panels.description: Mail and calendar events App Suite Middleware posts to /api/v1/webhook. 202: accepted and delivered to sockets and web push. 401: Middleware calls, but the webhook secret or signature is wrong. No line at all: Middleware stopped calling (for example a lost Dovecot push registration), so no user gets mail push. Matches the suggested SwitchboardNoMailWebhooks alert. The series only appears after a pod's first webhook.
panels.title: Webhook calls from App Suite Middleware (per minute, by status)
